content:
Tallulah Willis, the youngest of the actor’s three daughters with ex-wife Demi Moore, is apologizing for a photo she posted Saturday of herself and her dad that she thinks was “possibly too intimate” to share on social media.

The photo, which has since been deleted from Instagram, featured the father and daughter sitting on a porch swing. In the photo, screenshotted by People, the actor’s daughter is smiling and embracing her dad as he stares off into the distance, appearing confused.

The action star’s family announced in 2023 that he had been diagnosed with frontotemporal dementia after his prior diagnosis of aphasia progressed.

After deleting the post, the younger Willis published an Instagram Story on Sunday, screenshotted by TMZ, explaining her reasoning.

“I had someone take a super sweet photo of a shared moment between us watching a video of Frankie Valli singing,” she wrote in text over an old black-and-white photo of her dad kissing her when she was a kid. “I was very excited by the sweetness of the moment that I didn’t think farther ahead that this was possibly too intimate a photo to show.”

She continued, “I can acknowledge that and vow to do better. I know you all love him. I love him. My family loves him. And he’s still always the absolute hero we know him to be.”

It’s unclear how fans reacted to the original Instagram post, considering it has been deleted. But the polarizing photo Tallulah Willis posted over the weekend did make its way over to X. Some users there called it “sick” and claimed the photo was indicative of the family “exploiting” the Emmy-winner.

“The only part that is a real touchy grey area is Bruce himself,” another X user said, questioning whether the actor could truly consent to the photo. “Would HE want these photos of himself made public.”

Yet plenty of other X users disagreed.

This is also not the first time Tallulah Willis has received criticism for posting photos of her dad. In June 2025, she posted a carousel post on Instagram of herself holding her dad’s hand, hugging him, and the “Moonlighting” star posing with his daughter’s husband, Justin Acee.

“I don’t think you should expose your dad to the public! He is vulnerable! And some things should be kept private! You don’t have his permission to post it!” an Instagram user wrote of her 2025 post.

“Hi. I hear that. As a family we use our discretion when posting,” Tallulah Willis responded to the commenter. “Today was a great day filled with smiles. I made the [judgment] call to show that to the world, because I know what he means to everyone.”
